Signe Risom (also referred to as Signe Stelling Risom) is a cardiology nurse and PhD at Herlev and Gentofte Hospital [^src1]. She plays a significant role in the Danish healthcare system's approach to atrial fibrillation, specifically concerning patient education and quality improvement initiatives [^src1]. 

In the context of the 2025 AFDK (Atrieflimren i Danmark) report, Risom is recognized for her practical leadership in designing and implementing group teaching programs for patients newly diagnosed with atrial fibrillation [^src1]. Her work directly relates to the [[indikator-4a-implementation-at-herlev-og-gentofte-hospital]] at Herlev and Gentofte Hospital, which focuses on measuring and ensuring the quality of patient education [^src1]. 

Furthermore, Risom's expertise and clinical perspective have led to her inclusion in broader governance and oversight roles. She is a member of the [[afdk-styregruppe|Styregruppen for AFDK]], the steering group responsible for guiding the national quality and clinical development efforts for atrial fibrillation in Denmark [^src2]. Through her dual roles in hands-on clinical education and national steering, she bridges the gap between systemic quality measurement and direct patient care.
